open_points.subject: Room and ActingPrincipal
open_points.text: M03 says, “Who added it — the owner or the agent through Kernel — is not a fact of the room”; M07 says ActingPrincipal is recorded “on a room” and is “Embedded in audit entries, rooms and pointers.”
open_points.question: Does a Room store the acting principal that added it, or not?
options: A Room stores no acting principal.
A Room stores the ActingPrincipal that added it.
open_points.default_guess: A Room stores no acting principal, following M03's explicit round-1 closure.

open_points.subject: AuditEntry identity
open_points.text: M09 classifies AuditEntry as “entity” and says two entries with equal facts are distinct, but its list of facts contains no identity and does not say who mints or supplies one.
open_points.question: What gives each AuditEntry its distinct identity?
options: Registry mints an opaque AuditEntry id.
The event's position or sequence in the audit log is its identity.
AuditEntry is a value/event without a separately stored identity.
open_points.default_guess: Registry mints an opaque UUID for each AuditEntry.

open_points.subject: Audit entry for answering an access request
open_points.text: M09 includes “answering a request” among actions that write an entry, while R0-58 says Registry records only the listed significant changes, including “granting and revoking an agent session's projects,” and does not include declining or merely clearing a pending request.
open_points.question: Does every answer to an access request create an audit entry, including a decline that only clears the request, or is only an answer that grants a project audited as a grant?
options: Every grant or decline answer is audited.
Only an answer that grants a project is audited, as a grant.
No separate answer action is audited; any resulting grant or active-project change follows its own audit rule.
open_points.default_guess: Only an answer that grants a project is audited, as a grant.

open_points.subject: AuditEntry subject
open_points.text: M09 says the subject is “the project (`project_id`) or the customer (`customer_ref`) changed” and adds a session and project for a session grant, but it also requires entries for the import and erasing old audit entries; only the change bullet says the import's subject is M10, and no subject is stated for erasing old entries.
open_points.question: What subject fact does each import entry and old-audit-erasure entry carry, and may an AuditEntry have no project, customer or session subject?
options: Import uses MigrationClosure; old-entry erasure has no model subject and carries only the cutoff date.
Import uses MigrationClosure; old-entry erasure uses the audit log as a distinct subject kind.
Both actions use no subject beyond their action-specific facts.
Import entries instead name every imported project and customer.
open_points.default_guess: Import uses MigrationClosure, while old-entry erasure has no model subject and carries the cutoff date.

open_points.subject: Confirmation ids for confirmed no-op or refused actions
open_points.text: Identity formats says Registry mints a confirmation id when the owner confirms an action and “writes it once into the audit entry of that action,” including archiving and erasing an archived project. R0-12 and R0-71 allow confirmed no-op or refused cases—archiving an archived project returns it unchanged, anonymising an anonymised project returns it unchanged, and deleting an anonymised project is refused—while R0-58 and M09 describe the audit as changes of state and defer refused-attempt logging.
open_points.question: Is a confirmation id minted and an audit entry written when a confirmed action is a no-op or is refused?
options: Only a successful state-changing confirmation mints a retained confirmation id and audit entry.
Every confirmation mints an id and writes an audit entry, including no-ops and refusals.
Every confirmation mints an id, but no-op or refused confirmations are not necessarily retained in an audit entry.
open_points.default_guess: Only a successful state-changing confirmation mints a retained confirmation id and audit entry.

open_points.subject: MigrationClosure as a durable Registry model
open_points.text: State 0 says, “Registry stores only identity — projects, their objects and rooms, customers ... — the project access of each agent session and its pending request, artifact pointers, and its own audit log.” M10 adds a separate durable MigrationClosure record, and R0-24 says a new responsibility enters Registry only by a separate architecture decision.
open_points.question: Is the durable MigrationClosure an allowed additional Registry model despite State 0's exhaustive storage boundary, or must migration closure be represented using an already permitted fact such as the audit log or configuration?
options: Allow MigrationClosure as a separate durable model and amend State 0 accordingly.
Store migration closure only in the audit log.
Treat migration closure as configuration or another non-model operational marker.
open_points.default_guess: Allow the separate durable MigrationClosure and record an explicit State 0 amendment.
